mc-skills-001.front: Binoculars, spotting scope, rifle scope: the three jobs?
mc-skills-001.back: Binoculars find. Spotting scope judges. Rifle scope only aims (Tip). Never glass with the rifle scope: the muzzle follows your eye (95%).

mc-skills-003.front: Your pupil at dawn or dusk?
mc-skills-003.back: About 4 to 5 mm; in bright light 2 to 3 mm (85%, Vortex). Big exit pupils matter most in the first and last light.

mc-skills-004.back: 8x or 7x: Vortex calls them adequate for woodland; 10x for greater distances (85%).

mc-skills-006.front: How long does Josh Kirchner (onX) glass one spot?
mc-skills-006.back: About one hour at a time before moving (65%).

mc-skills-007.front: Glassing order: near first or far first?
mc-skills-007.back: Your call. Kirchner (onX): close and obvious first. Warren (Western Hunter): furthest points first, before heat haze (65%). Both: naked eye, quick pass, slow grid.

mc-skills-008.back: About a third of each binocular view (60%). Slow strips, then glass it all again.

mc-skills-009.front: Why glass far ground early in the day?
mc-skills-009.back: Heat waves (mirage) blur far slopes as the day warms (65%, Remi Warren).

mc-skills-010.front: Where should the sun be when you glass?
mc-skills-010.back: Behind you or to the side: the animal is lit, you are in shade (Tip).

mc-skills-011.back: A flat horizontal back line, the ear V, vertical leg poles, a flicker of movement. Also a white rump, an antler glint (65%).

mc-skills-012.back: Do not move. Keep eyes on it, pick two landmarks, judge it with the scope (Tip).

mc-skills-018.back: It was spooked, maybe by you. Walking tracks out: it left on its own (80%).

mc-skills-025.front: Plucked whole quills on a stump: who?
mc-skills-025.back: Likely a bird of prey. Bitten, wet, clumped feathers: a mammal (60%).

mc-skills-031.front: Following a track with your rifle is what, legally?
mc-skills-031.back: Hunting: following on the trail of wildlife with a firearm (95%). Hours and land rules apply.

mc-skills-032.back: No. An early 1990s estimate; experts think it may be low (65%, Outdoor Life 2026).

mc-skills-035.front: Which slopes flip uphill first, strongest, last?
mc-skills-035.back: East first, south strongest near midday, west by mid afternoon (75%).

mc-skills-036.back: About 5 to 13 km/h (3 to 8 mph). Downslope at night 3 to 8 km/h (75%).

mc-skills-050.back: Freeze, even on one leg, until it feeds again. Hold longer than it does (Tip).

mc-skills-053.back: Climbing up or down or getting in and out: about 60% (70%, Iowa DNR (Department of Natural Resources) with Tree Stand Safety Awareness).

mc-skills-056.back: Can occur in under 20 minutes and can be fatal (80%, Wisconsin DNR).

mc-skills-057.front: UW (University of Wisconsin) study: harness use among 117 injured stand hunters?
mc-skills-057.back: Only 4 reported any harness use; 55% of injuries involved the spine (75%).

mc-skills-059.back: Yes: not recorded or electronic (95%, my reading).

mc-skills-083.back: No bullet reliably goes through brush; a twig can throw the shot (70%, American Hunter).

mc-skills-084.back: Decide early, range landmarks, look at the spot not the antlers, breathe out; shaking hard means let it walk (60%, Tip).

mc-skills-085.front: Mule kick and hard low run after the shot?

mc-skills-086.back: Often a gut hit: mark it and back out for hours (70%).

mc-skills-112.back: Stop, Think, Observe, Plan. Doubt means stay (75%).

mc-skills-113.back: Anything in threes: whistle, mirror, horn, fires (75%).

mc-skills-114.front: First call when you need help?
mc-skills-114.back: 911 on any phone; any tower in range (75%). No signal: satellite SOS (65 to 85%).
